name: IL-16
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district lean of R+11
Incumbent LaHood with large financial advantage ($6.7M vs $230K cash)
No polls or expert ratings; markets price Republican win at ~97%
model.rationale: LaHood holds a heavily Republican seat with a dominant fundraising edge and no serious outside spending against him, while prediction markets price his reelection near certainty. The Democratic challenger's modest war chest gives no sign of a competitive race.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or unexpected outside spending against LaHood would be the main way this race tightens.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Darin LaHood seeks reelection in a central Illinois district that leans Republican by about eleven points, a structural advantage that makes a Democratic upset very unlikely. His challenger, Paul Nolley, has raised roughly $416,000 and holds about $230,000 on hand, while LaHood has built a war chest of $6.7 million with no meaningful outside opposition spending against him. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price a Republican win at roughly 97 percent. The forecast expects LaHood to win by a wide, double-digit margin, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling. Any meaningful competition would require an unforeseen development, as the district's lean, the incumbent's resources, and market pricing all point the same direction.
